name: Bangladesh
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Gopala founds the Pala dynasty
claims.summary: Gopala is raised to power amid disorder and founds the Pala dynasty, a Buddhist imperial line that would rule Bengal and Bihar for some four centuries and spread Buddhism as far as Tibet.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-750-gopala-founds-the-pala-dynasty, claim TL:BGD:event:750:gopala-founds-the-pala-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Somapura Mahavihara built at Paharpur
claims.summary: The Pala king Dharmapala builds the great monastery of Somapura at Paharpur, one of the largest Buddhist viharas south of the Himalayas and a centre of learning for centuries; today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sources.label: Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-800-somapura-mahavihara-built-at-paharpur, claim TL:BGD:event:800:somapura-mahavihara-built-at-paharpur, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Turkish conquest ends Sena rule
claims.summary: The general Bakhtiyar Khalji conquers Bengal, ending the Hindu Sena dynasty and inaugurating centuries of Muslim rule in the delta.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1204-turkish-conquest-ends-sena-rule, claim TL:BGD:event:1204:turkish-conquest-ends-sena-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iliyas Shah founds the Bengal Sultanate
claims.summary: Shamsuddin Iliyas Shah unifies Bengal's principalities and establishes the independent Iliyas Shahi Sultanate at Lakhnauti, beginning more than two centuries of sovereign Muslim rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1342-iliyas-shah-founds-the-bengal-sultanate, claim TL:BGD:event:1342:iliyas-shah-founds-the-bengal-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Husain Shah
claims.summary: Alauddin Husain Shah presides over a golden age of the Bengal Sultanate, patronising Bengali literature and extending the kingdom's frontiers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1494-reign-of-husain-shah, claim TL:BGD:event:1494:reign-of-husain-shah, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mughal conquest of Bengal
claims.summary: Akbar's forces defeat the last independent sultan at the Battle of Rajmahal, ending the Bengal Sultanate and absorbing the delta into the Mughal Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1576-mughal-conquest-of-bengal, claim TL:BGD:event:1576:mughal-conquest-of-bengal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dhaka becomes the Mughal capital of Bengal
claims.summary: The Mughal governor establishes Dhaka as the capital of the Bengal subah, and the city grows into a hub of administration, military power and the global muslin trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1610-dhaka-becomes-the-mughal-capital-of-bengal, claim TL:BGD:event:1610:dhaka-becomes-the-mughal-capital-of-bengal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dhaka muslin and the wealth of Bengal
claims.summary: Mughal Bengal becomes the world's foremost exporter of fine muslin and a leading source of European trade with Asia, making the province the richest in the empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1700-dhaka-muslin-and-the-wealth-of-bengal, claim TL:BGD:event:1700:dhaka-muslin-and-the-wealth-of-bengal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The nawabs of Bengal become autonomous
claims.summary: As Mughal central power fades after Aurangzeb's death, the governors of Bengal rule as near-independent nawabs over the empire's wealthiest province.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1717-the-nawabs-of-bengal-become-autonomous, claim TL:BGD:event:1717:the-nawabs-of-bengal-become-autonomous, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Plassey
claims.summary: Robert Clive's East India Company forces defeat Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah after the betrayal of Mir Jafar, beginning British political control of Bengal and, in time, of India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1757-battle-of-plassey, claim TL:BGD:event:1757:battle-of-plassey, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Bengal Famine
claims.summary: An estimated ten million people — about a third of Bengal's population — die as monsoon failure compounds the East India Company's insistence on collecting land revenue from a starving peasantry.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1770-the-great-bengal-famine, claim TL:BGD:event:1770:the-great-bengal-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Partition of Bengal
claims.summary: Viceroy Lord Curzon divides Bengal into a Muslim-majority east (capital Dacca) and a Hindu-majority west, sparking the Swadeshi movement; the partition is annulled in 1911.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1905-first-partition-of-bengal, claim TL:BGD:event:1905:first-partition-of-bengal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Partition creates East Pakistan
claims.summary: The partition of British India makes Muslim-majority eastern Bengal into East Pakistan, a wing of the new state separated from its western half by a thousand miles of India.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1947-partition-creates-east-pakistan, claim TL:BGD:event:1947:partition-creates-east-pakistan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bengali Language Movement
claims.summary: Students in Dhaka demanding that Bengali be a state language of Pakistan are shot by police; the martyrs become foundational to Bengali nationalism and, later, to UNESCO's International Mother Language Day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1952-the-bengali-language-movement, claim TL:BGD:event:1952:the-bengali-language-movement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Awami League's Six-Point demand
claims.summary: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's Awami League issues a six-point programme for the political and economic autonomy of East Pakistan, the charter of Bengali self-determination.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1966-the-awami-league-s-six-point-demand, claim TL:BGD:event:1966:the-awami-league-s-six-point-demand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Awami League wins the election
claims.summary: The Awami League secures 167 of the 169 East Pakistani seats and a National Assembly majority; West Pakistan's refusal to hand over power ignites the crisis that leads to war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1970-awami-league-wins-the-election, claim TL:BGD:event:1970:awami-league-wins-the-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Declaration of independence
claims.summary: After the Pakistani army launches Operation Searchlight on 25 March, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman proclaims Bangladesh's independence on 26 March, beginning the Liberation War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1971-declaration-of-independence, claim TL:BGD:event:1971:declaration-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Victory and the birth of Bangladesh
claims.summary: After a nine-month war in which possibly a million Bengalis were killed and ten million fled to India, Indian forces intervene and the Pakistani army surrenders at Dhaka, founding the People's Republic of Bangladesh.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1971-victory-and-the-birth-of-bangladesh, claim TL:BGD:event:1971:victory-and-the-birth-of-bangladesh, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Mujib and military rule
claims.summary: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and most of his family are killed in a coup; a counter-coup brings Ziaur Rahman to power, beginning fifteen years of military-dominated rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-1975-assassination-of-mujib-and-military-rule, claim TL:BGD:event:1975:assassination-of-mujib-and-military-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 2024 uprising and Hasina's fall
claims.summary: A student-led mass uprising over a civil-service job-quota system forces Sheikh Hasina to resign after fifteen years and flee to India; the Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus is appointed to head an interim government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bangladesh: From Buddhist Bengal and the wealth of the Mughals to the nation born in 1971.", terralore.co/country/BGD/chronicle#ev-2024-the-2024-uprising-and-hasina-s-fall, claim TL:BGD:event:2024:the-2024-uprising-and-hasina-s-fall, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
